My general advice is to invest more time in your interests and in serving others. Also, you should take the attitude that you will address the challenges before you. For me, the more directly I address situations in my life when I am in a rut, the more satisfied and less anxious I feel. Finally, I would try to prioritize time spent in the real world meeting people versus spending time online (voat excepted, of course!).

My more specific advice is as follows:

  • You mentioned that you learned to cook and bake properly, but that there were no jobs at present. In that case, I would still spend time cooking (even if it is volunteering to cook for others) until such jobs are available. This will keep your skills sharp and your mind occuppied. Maybe there is a caterer in the area who could hire you for certain events. Maybe you could volunteer to cook for friends and neighbors and get a free meal in exchange. Actively look for opportunities to cook for others.

  • Join a local organization, preferably something you care about but even something that is mildly interesting to you. You don't have to commit to anything full time, but I would attend events and meetings and just be around other people in real life.

  • Along the same lines, I would look for ways to volunteer for others. Beyond the obvious altruistic value, volunteering generally makes you feel good about yourself, gives you added confidence, and is another good way to meet people.

  • Even if you do everything I stated above, that will leave you plenty of time for the other interest you mentioned, LoL. I don't know much about this but if it floats your goat, go for it!!!
